description: Two-panel composite figure reporting the mechanical behaviour of two low-alloy ultrahigh-strength steels before and after tempering at 180 °C. (a) Engineering stress-strain curves with Engineering Stress /MPa on the y-axis (0-3000, ticks every 500) and Engineering Strain on the x-axis (0-16, ticks every 2; no unit printed). Four curves are drawn: solid blue = 0Al, WQ; dashed blue = 0Al, 2h; solid magenta = 1.3Al, WQ; dashed magenta = 1.3Al, 2h. The two as-quenched curves rise steeply to the highest stresses: the 0Al, WQ curve climbs above the 2000 MPa gridline, peaks near 2300 MPa between strain ~8 and ~9, then falls to about 2100 MPa at strain ~10. The 1.3Al, WQ curve peaks near 2150 MPa at strain ~4.3 and is truncated there, terminating well before the other curves — the fracture-before-maximum-strength behaviour. Both 2h-tempered dashed curves are lower, peaking near 1900-1950 MPa around strain 8-9 and extending to strain ~14 at roughly 1250-1300 MPa. (b) A bar chart of KU2 /J (0-100, ticks every 20) versus Samples: 0Al,WQ = 33 J, 0Al,2h = 65 J, 1.3Al,WQ = 23 J, 1.3Al,2h = 80 J, each with error bars. Together the panels show that tempering trades ~300-400 MPa of strength for a marked gain in impact toughness, with the Al-bearing steel giving the largest toughness gain.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves for four conditions (0Al, WQ; 0Al, 2h; 1.3Al, WQ; 1.3Al, 2h). Y-axis Engineering Stress/MPa (0-3000), x-axis Engineering Strain (0-16). The 0Al, WQ solid curve reaches the highest stress (peak between the 2000 and 2500 gridlines, just above 2000 at ~2300 MPa region) and ends near strain 10. The 1.3Al, WQ solid curve is the shortest, terminating at strain ~4.3 just after its peak near 2150 MPa. The two dashed 2h curves peak near 1900-1950 MPa and extend to strain ~14, ending near 1250-1300 MPa.

Bar chart of KU2 impact absorbing energy in J (y-axis, 0-100 with ticks every 20) for Samples: 0Al,WQ (33 J), 0Al,2h (65 J), 1.3Al,WQ (23 J) and 1.3Al,2h (80 J). Bars are purple with black error bars; values are printed above each bar.

observations.observation: Panel (a) legend entries are exactly '0Al, WQ' (solid blue), '0Al, 2h' (dashed blue), '1.3Al, WQ' (solid magenta) and '1.3Al, 2h' (dashed magenta).

In panel (a) the 0Al, WQ curve reaches the highest engineering stress of the four, peaking between the 2000 and 2500 MPa gridlines at engineering strain between about 8 and 9, then dropping to about 2100 MPa at strain ~10.

In panel (a) the 1.3Al, WQ curve terminates at an engineering strain of about 4-4.5, immediately after its peak just above the 2000 MPa gridline, i.e. it is truncated before the other curves reach their maxima.

In panel (a) both 2h-tempered dashed curves (0Al, 2h and 1.3Al, 2h) lie below the as-quenched curves, peak near the 2000 MPa gridline (between 1500 and 2000 for most of their length), and extend to an engineering strain of ~14 ending near 1250-1300 MPa.
Panel (b) prints the KU2 values above each bar: 33 for 0Al,WQ, 65 for 0Al,2h, 23 for 1.3Al,WQ and 80 for 1.3Al,2h (units J as given by the axis label KU2/J).
Panel (b) shows error bars on all four bars, so the printed values are means with a spread; the 1.3Al,2h bar has the widest visible upper error bar reaching ~80 J.
The caption states the figure reports mechanical properties of the two steels before and after tempering at 180 °C, with (a) engineering stress-strain curves and (b) impact absorbing energy.

The citing text states the as-quenched UTS/YS were 2294 ± 9 MPa and 1234 ± 22 MPa for the 0Al steel and 2145 ± 144 MPa and 1113 ± 11 MPa for the 1.3Al steel, with total elongations of 9.5 ± 0.6 % and 4.3 ± 0.9 % respectively (values not printed on the figure).
The citing text states that the 1.3Al steel fractured prior to reaching its maximum tensile strength during the tensile test, which matches the early truncation of the 1.3Al, WQ curve in panel (a).

The citing text states that after tempering the UTS and YS fell to 1925 ± 5 MPa / 1400 ± 12 MPa (0Al) and 1876 ± 25 MPa / 1272 ± 52 MPa (1.3Al), both below 2000 MPa, while total elongation rose to 13.5 ± 1.8 % and 13.7 ± 0.4 % respectively.

The citing text states KU2 increased from 33 ± 6 J to 65 ± 3 J for the 0Al steel after 2 h tempering, and from 23 ± 2 J to approximately 80 ± 3 J for the 1.3Al steel, an improvement of about 3.5 times; these match the printed bar values 33, 65, 23 and 80.
